**Reading map:** Deisenroth, Faisal & Ong, *Mathematics for Machine Learning* (2020), §3.6. This is an original lesson using our delivery-operations example—not reproduced textbook content.

## Why the concept matters

Some changes are represented by a chosen model subspace and others remain unexplained. The orthogonal complement collects directions perpendicular to every vector in that subspace.

## Define the mathematical relationship

$$
V^\perp=\{\boldsymbol z:\langle\boldsymbol z,\boldsymbol v\rangle=0\ \forall\boldsymbol v\in V\}
$$

The displayed relationship is the main object to analyse. Specify the relevant dimensions, quantities and assumptions before using it. It should be read as a mathematical statement, not merely a programming shorthand.

## Work through an original example

If V=span((1,1)) in R^2, then V-perp=span((1,-1)). Their dot product is zero. Every vector in R^2 can be decomposed into parts along these two independent directions.

## What follows, and what does not

With ordinary least squares, the fitted values belong to the design matrix's column space and the residual is orthogonal to it when the minimum is attained.

## Test your reasoning

Find one nonzero vector orthogonal to (2,1).
